parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Describe the role of DNA in the production of systemin.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Systemin stimulates plant cells to produce enzyme inhibitors known as serpins.
One of these serpins is a competitive inhibitor of some protease enzymes. It inhibits the
protease enzymes found in herbivores, but does not inhibit the proteases in plants.
Suggest how this serpin inhibits only the protease enzymes in herbivores but not those
in plants.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
The presence of competitive inhibitors, such as serpins, increases the Michaelis-Menten
constant (K ) for the enzymes they inhibit.
Explain why the K value increases.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the process of DNA replication.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
State the name of the part of the chromosome that prevents the loss of genes during DNA
replication.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
During DNA replication, the use of an incorrect base in the newly synthesised strand can lead
to a mutation.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
A transversion event is where a pyrimidine is used in the newly synthesised strand
instead of a purine, or the other way round.
Name the two possible bases that could be used instead of cytosine in a transversion
event.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
A transition event is where an incorrect purine is used or an incorrect pyrimidine is used.
Suggest why transversion events are less likely to occur than transition events.
